title: CI runs at milestones, not on every merge, and you get options on best practice
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 (waiting page, item 27): "Not only drop the exception, I merge so arbitrarily and can merge so often that frankly I still find the amount of CI used to be preposterous. I think there may be something in this roadmap already of essentially wanting \"milestone-style\" reviews of CI -- I think my Q_Max repo might have some examples of that where I got so sick of my CI bill that I was like look orchestrator after u see a ton has landed then yes run a check but not every merge. That could be me not doing best practices, and I'm eager to learn, and/but I want some help here"
note: Measured Oct 13-27 at main 2ad85de: about 16,800 runner-minutes a week; the run after each merge to main is 38% of it and ended green 4 of 48 times last week, mostly cut off at Windows and Chromium time caps. Item 27 (c69) answered a: drop the per-lane full CI job exception; the build advisor has it. Part 1 done Oct 27 (doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/XMDQP1nVCuq3u35qvwE8eV). Ruling, Oct 27 12:07 CDT (shiv, item 31): (e), trust first then cut in steps, "a combo of a, c, e". Reading built from it: step 1 is (e): the full run stops timing out, a mutation check measures test value, and merges that needed a repair are counted; step 2 takes q_max's shape (a: quick checks on each branch, full suite on main) in place of (b); step 3 ends at (c)'s milestone runs. Each step starts only past its measured bar, and a missed bar steps back. Step 1 lanes queue with the build advisor. The rule lands in the global CLAUDE.md (roles-each-layer-proves-once, git-integration-branch-merge) and the gates workflows. Port: yes; the rule is global, each repo's workflows follow at its visit. Placed ahead of c82, after c88 (triage, Oct 27): CI spend grows with every merge.
